Encomium

en-KOH-mee-uhm · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing expressing high praise.

The retiring professor's colleagues wrote a lengthy encomium praising her four decades of research.

Worked Example

At the retirement dinner, his former students delivered a heartfelt encomium celebrating his decades of teaching.

An encomium is a formal tribute, usually spoken or written for a specific occasion honoring someone's achievements.

How Encomium Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tribute

tribute: an act or statement showing respect or admiration

commendation

commendation: an official expression of praise

Antonyms

criticism

criticism: the expression of disapproval

condemnation

condemnation: a strong expression of disapproval

How Strong Is It? — compliment → encomium → commemoration

compliment vs. encomium

compliment vs. encomium: A compliment can be a single sentence; an encomium is a full, formal piece of praise.

commemoration vs. encomium

commemoration vs. encomium: A commemoration marks and honors a specific occasion or person even more formally and ceremonially than an everyday encomium.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — en-

prefix — en-: in, within (Greek)

root — com

root — com: revel, celebration (Greek (komos))

suffix — -ium

suffix — -ium: noun-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: en- ("in") + com ("revel, celebration") + -ium (noun ending) = a piece written within the spirit of celebration -- a formal tribute.

Use the root in a new word: comedy

Use the root in a new word: comedy: That same Greek "komos" root (revel, celebration) is also hidden inside the everyday word "comedy."
